title: Representation Learning for Equivariant Inference with Guarantees
claim: Our symmetry-aware method is more sample-efficient and yields better-calibrated uncertainty than baselines on a real robotics task.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: sample-efficiency plot, robot photo, 4x2 grid of CI time-series
description: The figure has three parts in a row. On the left is a log-log line plot of MSE against number of training samples, with a title giving the symmetry group. Four models appear in the legend: eNCP in teal, NCP in navy, eMLP in orange and MLP in red. Shaded bands show variance. The teal eNCP line is lowest and drops steadily. In the middle is a render of a black quadruped robot on a checkered floor. Green arrows mark the feet and cyan and orange arrows mark momentum. On the right is a grid of small time-series plots. Rows are eNCP, NCP, eCQR and CQR. Columns are U[J] and T[J]. Each plot shows a blue ground-truth line, a light-red confidence band and red outlier dots. The eNCP row has few red outliers, while the other rows have many.
caption: Left: Test set sample efficiency for $\G$-equivariant regression (MSE vs. training samples) when predicting the $\G$-equivariant linear and angular momentum of a quadruped robot’s center of mass (\acrshort{com}) from noisy joint positions and velocities. Right: Uncertainty quantification via $\G$-equivariant prediction of $90%$ \glspl{ci} (light-red area) for the robot's instantaneous work $U_t$ and kinetic energy $T_t$ during locomotion over rough terrain for our method (\acrshort{encp}) and competitors. The figure shows a trajectory with a strong initial disturbance, where blue markers denote samples within the predicted CI and red markers denote those outside. Note that only \acrshort{encp} is able to predict well-calibrated CI intervals that cover both the disturbance and recovery phases.
abstract: In many real-world applications of regression, conditional probability estimation, and uncertainty quantification, exploiting symmetries rooted in physics or geometry can dramatically improve generalization and sample efficiency. While geometric deep learning has made empirical advances by incorporating symmetry and geometry priors, less attention has been given to statistical learning guarantees. In this paper, we introduce an equivariant representation learning framework that simultaneously addresses regression, conditional probability estimation, and uncertainty quantification while providing first-of-its-kind non-asymptotic statistical learning guarantees. Grounded in operator and group representation theory, our framework approximates the spectral decomposition of the conditional expectation operator, building representations that are both equivariant and disentangled along independent symmetry quotient groups. Empirical evaluations on synthetic datasets and real-world robotics applications confirm the potential of our approach, matching or outperforming existing equivariant baselines in regression while providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates.
